text.p: MedPartners Inc said on Tuesday that it is re-evaluating the terms of its January merger agreement with InPhyNet Medical Management Inc to call for a downward adjustment in the agreement's exchange ratio.
The merger agreement originally set an exchange ratio of 1.311 shares of MedPartners' stock for every share of InPhyNet stock, MedPartners said.

The re-evaluation comes after InPhyNet revised its year-end 1996 earnings and earnings for the quarter ended March 31 to reflect a change in the accounting for costs associated with a five-year agreement with Physician Corp of America.
"With the change in the accounting method required by the SEC, MedPartners believes that a downward adjustment in the exchange ratio is required," MedPartners said in a statement.
MedPartners is a physician management organization.
MedPartners announced on January 21 that it had agreed to merge with InPhyNet in a deal valued at $493 million.
MedPartners also said that the combined company would have $5.2 billion in revenues and that it would be the largest provider of full-time hospital-based physician services.
No one was immediately available at InPhyNet to comment on the merger re-evaluation, or to discuss its earnings figures.
MedPartners said the companies were continuing discussions towards reaching a modified agreement.
